newsitem.title: UK: UK property stocks rise on inflation hedge appeal.
newsitem.headline: UK property stocks rise on inflation hedge appeal.

text.p: Property companies shares gained ground, beckoning investors on election day as protection against inflation - historically a corollary of a Labour government, dealers and analysts said.

The market reacted to signs that opposition Labour's victory in Thursday's election looked increasingly sure, they said. Land Securities Plc put on 4p to 805-1/2p, MEPC Plc gained 8-1/2p to 461-1/2p and Chelsfield Plc rose 8p to 361-1/2p.

"The latest IG Index poll shows the Labour majority creeping higher and in the general melee of the market today people are buying property stocks as the traditional inflation hedge," said one analyst.
The IG Index estimated a Labour majority between 96 and 106 seats.
"We don't think they are necessarily a good hedge against inflation or that a Labour government would necessarily push inflation higher," he said.
But analysts said that historically Labour government's have also brought in higher development taxes and planning curbs, pushing rents up.
"These look like good defensive buys and anyway there's a greater feeling of optimism around generally in the rental market," said another analyst.
